issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for a landlord’s suit to recover possession from a tenant under rent-control protections is governed by the specific provisions for possession suits, rather than the residual limitation provision.
material_facts: The landlord sued to recover possession from a tenant, alleging permanent alterations and acts of waste and damage that were grounds for eviction under the rent-control statute.
The trial court found the eviction grounds established and decreed possession.
The appellate court dismissed the suit as time-barred under the residual three-year limitation provision; the High Court set that decision aside.
The appeals challenged only the applicable limitation period and the accrual of the cause of action.
The possession suit was filed within twelve years of the relevant trigger for limitation.
issues.conclusion: The limitation statute applied, but the suit fell under either the provision governing a landlord’s suit against a tenant after determination of the tenancy or the provision governing possession after forfeiture or breach of condition. The applicable period was twelve years, not three years, and the suit was not time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: The limitation statute is not inherently inapplicable to possession suits under rent-control legislation. The provisions protecting tenants from eviction and allowing eviction on specified grounds must be read harmoniously. Under the limitation statute, the provision for a landlord’s suit to recover possession from a tenant applies when the tenancy is determined; alternatively, the provision for possession following forfeiture or breach may apply. Either provision displaces the residual provision. The Court applied Haji Suleman Haji Ayub Bhiwandiwala v. Narayan Sadashiv Ogale on the coexistence and harmonious construction of the rent-control provisions, and considered Dhanpal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal, Pradesh Kumar Bajpai v. Binod Behari Sarkar, and Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar on eviction under rent legislation and determination of tenancy.

rule.if: landlord_tenant_possession_suit and rent_control_eviction_protection_applies and statutory_eviction_ground_established and suit_filed_within_applicable_twelve_year_period

predicates.landlord_tenant_possession_suit: A landlord brought a suit to recover possession of property from a tenant.
predicates.rent_control_eviction_protection_applies: The tenant’s protection against eviction was governed by rent-control legislation.
predicates.statutory_eviction_ground_established: The court found that the tenant had committed conduct that constituted a statutory ground for eviction.
predicates.suit_filed_within_applicable_twelve_year: The landlord brought the possession suit within twelve years of the relevant event from which the applicable limitation period ran.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a possession suit against a tenant covered by rent-control protections, a statutory eviction ground is established, and the suit is filed within the applicable twelve-year period, the suit is not time-barred.
